text:
alex: seeing a big spike in 502s from the hosted inference API starting ~2350001200. Errors look tied to ratekeeper/quota returning 5xx under burst.

ops-bot: alert — quota-service latency > 5s, error-rate 18% over last 5m :rotating_light:

jordan: on it. do we have a correlation with heartbeat or kv-cache pressure? any recent deploys?

sarah: no deploys in the window. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/kv/rlimit — trying to paste top graphs:
```
ratekeeper.heartbeat.latency.p95 = 4.6s
quota.request.latency.p95 = 6.2s
quota.5xx.rate = 18%
kv.cache.hit = 42%
```

kate (support): customer X reported ~4000 failed requests in last hour, billing shows retries and doubled token usage. customer on a reserved-dedicated plan, they're pretty upset.

mike-support: repro steps from my curl:
```
# hammer endpoint with concurrent connections
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":64}' &
done
```
I see intermittent 502/500 within ~10s. logs show: "quota-orch: downstream timeout waiting for ratekeeper heartbeat"

alex: interesting — logs also show counter-sync errors: "counter-store stale: last-write 45s ago". Ratekeeper heartbeat appears delayed when under p99 throughput. Could be a lock around kv counter flush.

jordan: can you drop a minimal log snippet? also whats the exact error string the edge returns? we should classify whether it's dependency-timeout vs internal classifier fallback.

sarah: paste from logs (sanitized):
```
[2350001278] quota-orch ERROR: heartbeat wait exceeded 3000ms, upstream rpc timeout
[2350001281] quota-orch WARN: counters stale=true last_write_delta_ms=45321
[2350001284] quota-orch ERROR: returning 502 instead of 429 due to misroute in error-handling path
```

kate (support): customer wants mitigation asap. any immediate workaround to reduce errors? they can reduce client concurrency but we need platform side mitigation.

alex: ops mitigation idea: enable local short-circuit that converts dependency-timeout into 429 for quota checks (hotfix toggle) — that will appease customers and avoid 5xx. toggling now will also bypass the stale counter sync for short term.

jordan: agree. I'll open a small canary: config patch to classify upstream timeouts -> 429 when origin is ratekeeper. patch:
```
- if upstream == ratekeeper && err.type == Timeout => respond 429
+ if upstream == ratekeeper && err.type == Timeout => respond 429 (config: classify-ratekeeper-timeouts=true)
```
I'll roll to canary in eu-west-1 first.

mike-support: can you add an alert on "counters.stale > 10s" and a synthetic test that hits quota during bursts? will help catch regressions for customer.

sarah: added alert rule, created synthetic runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.local/rlimit-heartbeat-stale. Also investigating kv write path: suspect locking during flush to disk under mem-pressure.

alex: long term: we should make quota checks resilient to heartbeat latency (local cache fallback + best-effort token accounting + async reconcile). but short-term canary should reduce 5xxs.

jordan: rolling canary now -> canary deployed at 2350001500. monitoring...

ops-bot: canary metrics: quota.5xx.rate dropped from 18% -> 2.3% in eu-west-1 within 3m :white_check_mark:

kate (support): update to customer: we rolled a targeted canary to reduce 5xxs, working on root cause (heartbeat/counter flush). asked them to temporarily throttle clients to <100 concurrency if they still see issues.

sarah: root cause hypothesis: large concurrent traffic caused kv counter flush to stall (GC/IO), heartbeat queued behind flush, downstream timeout -> error-handling path returned 502. next steps: add non-blocking flush, metrics on kv-flush queue length, and add robust fallback accounting.

alex: filing followup ticket in infra backlog with priority P1, will include repro harness, traces, and design for non-blocking counter writes. thanks everyone. :pray:
